title: Mitigate TTFT spike: kernel heuristic fallback & model routing mitigation
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Summary:
Customer escalations started on 2026-03-12 after multiple tenants observed a 2x-5x degradation in time-to-first-token (TTFT) and a sustained drop in tokens/sec across Hosted, Dedicated, and Private clusters. Affected model families reported in initial reports: Llama-3-8b-chat variants, a 7B quantized family, and a small set of custom customer-uploaded models that share the same attention kernels. Symptoms are elevated scheduler queue times, CPU-side kernel selection stalls, and increased tail latency on the first token generation path (warm and cold starts).

Impact and scope:
- Immediate customer impact: degraded real-time chat experiences (timeouts, delayed first token).
- Observed across all environments (hosted, dedicated pools, private deployments that pulled runtime-1.22).
- Spike started ~2026-03-12 09:45 UTC, coincident with rollout of small scheduler heuristic change (commit 3f9d4a2).

Investigation highlights:
- Correlation found between the scheduler heuristic change and increased time spent in kernel selection code path (profiler traces: Flamegraph: https://grafana.redwood.internal/d/rt/scheduler-flame?from=now-2h).
- Kernel selector now prefers a unified FP16 path for models that previously used a mixed quantized kernel. Under certain seq-length distributions this caused extra fallback checks and a higher probability of selecting non-optimal kernels, which increases CPU work and blocks the GPU dispatch pipeline.
- KV-cache warm path appears unaffected; issue predominantly affects first-token scheduling and short-chat patterns (seq_len <= 64).

Immediate mitigations implemented (today):
1) Canary rollback of scheduler heuristic on a small portion of hosted traffic (canary id: canary-rt-17321).
2) Emergency routing rule added to Console to route high-priority customer traffic to model variant with pre-verified kernel mapping (route name: rt/mitigate/17321).
3) Temporary reduction of per-worker batch window for short-sequence requests to avoid long head-of-line blocking.

Proposed permanent fixes and plan:
- Short term (next 48h): ship patch to kernel selector to add a fast-path for short seq_len and skip expensive fallback checks when model metadata indicates quantized-compatible layers (PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/2445).
- Mid term (2 weeks): add unit and integration tests to the kernel selection harness to simulate distributions (short-chat heavy) and assert no regressions on TTFT metrics.
- Long term: implement a telemetry-driven auto-tuning layer that selects kernel profiles per model and per-traffic-pattern, persisted to a model-profile cache to avoid runtime checks.

Customer comms:
- Notified top-affected customers in thread #inc-ttft-17321 on Slack and opened support tickets: ACME (#SUP-9981), FinCore (#SUP-9982).
- Drafted status email to impacted customers with ETA for hotpatch and follow-up retrospective.

Acceptance criteria for closing ticket:
- End-to-end TTFT for the affected models returns to baseline (within 10%) in hosted and dedicated clusters for both p50/p95 across short-chat workloads.
- Canary to full rollout conversion plan validated with rolling metrics and no new regressions in tokens/sec.
- Post-mortem published documenting root cause, PRs, and checklist to prevent recurrence.
